1.28.8: On Today, every class whose lesson has slides now has a Present button, not only the class on now. Two classes sharing one lesson can each present it.

While presenting, Pop out (or W) puts the slides in a window of their own for a second screen or projector. That window shows only what the class sees, and this one keeps the bar, your notes and the timer. The keys work in either window.
1.28.7: Save a screenshot as a strong example: tick “Save as a strong example” in the Screenshot bar, or press the button on the “Picture copied” note. Before it is saved you can black out anything, like a name, and add why it’s strong and tags.

The Examples page finds work again by tag or by searching what you wrote. Every card shows its tags, and you can change them from its ⋯ menu. Download as a sheet works for whatever the page is showing.
1.28.6: In another language, the boxes a class page opens now read in that language too: a new or changed assignment, the roster, units, how the class is graded, Email wording and report Wording, the notes pages for work with no papers, and the progress sheets you print.
Class, unit, assignment and student names, and the sentences in the Wording boxes, stay as you typed them. The marking screen and its boxes are still in English.
1.28.5: In another language, the rest of a class page now reads in that language: a student’s own page, Charts, Goals and Report comments, and the gradebook, charts and levels of a class graded with IB criteria. Pointing at a mark on a chart says it in that language too. Names, rubric rows, goals and criteria stay as you typed them.
A report comment’s draft is still written in English until you put your own sentences in Wording…. The boxes that open from these tabs are still in English.
Fixed in German: “Grade” showed as “Notiz” in a few places, and now reads “Note”.
1.28.4: In another language, more of a class page now reads in that language: the Gradebook, Students, Attendance, Seating and Missing work tabs, with dates written that language’s way and your own names left as you typed them.
Still in English: a student’s own page, Charts, Goals, Report comments, the gradebook of a class graded with IB criteria, and the boxes that open from these tabs.
1.28.3: In another language, a class page now reads in that language too: its header, its row of tabs and the Assignments tab, with your own class, unit and assignment names left as you typed them. The Gradebook and the other tabs are still in English.
1.28.2: Settings is now in your language too: all seven pages, in each of the eight languages. Help answers name the Settings buttons the way Settings shows them.
Boxes that open from Settings, such as Term setup and the mark key, are still in English, and so are the class and marking screens.
1.28.1: The app opens a little faster at its web address: it now fetches only the language you chose instead of carrying all of them. Your language is kept for use without internet, and the take-home file still has every language inside.
1.28.0: Six more app languages: Simplified Chinese (简体中文), French, German, Portuguese, Japanese and Korean, beside Traditional Chinese and Spanish. Choose one in Settings, Display, App language.
Each covers the same first screens: the sidebar, Today, the welcome, Find anything, Help and the feedback page students get. The other screens are still in English.
None of the translations has been checked by a fluent speaker yet, so a line may read oddly.
1.27.36: IB MYP classes: Quick mark now gives levels for a paper quiz. On the boxes screen each question counts for one criterion, and under Points to levels you type the lowest points that earn each level. The quiz then gives a level for each criterion, with no total and no percent.
1.27.35: IB DP classes: the Grading box now has Components, where each type of work (Paper 1, the internal assessment and so on) gets its own weight for that class alone. In the Gradebook, More has Predicted grades: click the 1 to 7 you predict for each student, with the grade the percent earns outlined as a hint. Predicted grades show in the gradebook and on progress sheets.
1.27.34: A class page is simpler. The tab row has Assignments, Gradebook, Students and More; the pin beside a page in More keeps it in the row. Roster, grading and the class link are under one Class setup button.
The gradebook has one More menu for Term setup, extra credit, import and copy. Settings has seven pages in place of twelve, and nothing has been removed.
In the Planner’s week, Use a lesson shows when you point at a class slot.
1.27.33: Every activity in the Planner’s Activities bank has a video button. See it in action opens a short classroom video of it from sources such as Edutopia, EL Education and Reading Rockets; where there isn’t a good one, Find a video searches YouTube for it. Your own activities can carry a video link, and the link goes into the speaker notes when you add an activity to a lesson.
1.27.32: IB MYP classes: report comments are drafted from the levels you set and the 1 to 7, and a progress sheet shows each criterion’s level, the total, the grade and every task’s levels, with no percent. A new year keeps a class’s criteria and boundaries and leaves the students’ levels behind. My setup now brings an MYP teacher in as IB MYP criteria.
1.27.31: A lesson in the Planner is tidier under the slide. This slide has your speaker notes beside one box for your AI assistant. The whole lesson has Materials, Links, Finished PowerPoint, comments and Taught as matching cards.
The tips for editing a slide are behind an Editing tips button, and Alternative version is in More until a lesson has more than one version.
1.27.30: A lesson in the Planner has a Links box for the web pages you open while teaching it. Paste an address, or pick one from School resources.
A School resource can be for one class. Its links then show on every lesson for that class, and in Present under Links (the L key).
1.27.29: IB MYP tasks: the Grades tab shows each criterion’s level with no total or percent, and Copy all levels copies them. Insights leaves out the percent tiles, and text shared with an assistant says the rows are levels, not points to add up. Help has two new answers, for IB MYP and IB DP.
1.27.28: Coming from Google Classroom? Settings, Classes and rosters has a new button, From Google Classroom…. Choose the grades file you download from Classroom and it makes the class with its students, then shows every assignment and score for you to check before they go into the gradebook. A folder of student work downloaded from Google Drive now opens with each student’s files together. Nothing is sent anywhere and there is no sign-in. Help has an answer for it.
1.27.27: Screenshot: press S on a paper, Alt S (⌥S on a Mac) anywhere, or the button at the foot of the marking tools. Drag over what you want, click a page for the whole page, or press Enter for the whole screen, and the picture is copied, ready to paste. On a paper, name covers stay painted in and the student’s name and file name are left off; With my marks chooses whether your marks come too.
1.27.26: Full screen: press F, or Full screen near the bottom of the sidebar (beside ✕ while a paper is open). The browser’s bars go away and the sidebar folds to icons, or goes while you mark, so the paper gets the room. F again, the same button or Esc leaves, and nothing is closed or lost. On formative work F is for feedback, so use the button there.
1.27.25: IB classes. Each class has a Grading button: points and percent, IB MYP or IB DP. The welcome and Settings offer IB MYP criteria (0 to 8) and IB DP 1 to 7 as two separate choices.

An MYP class is marked against the criteria a task assesses, each 0 to 8, with no percent. Its gradebook shows every level a student earned, you choose the level that fits best for each criterion, and the total becomes a final grade of 1 to 7. Levels are never averaged.
Criterion names and the grade boundaries are yours to change. A DP class shows the 1 to 7 its percent earns on boundaries you type in.
1.27.24: My setup, in Settings: copy a prompt into your AI assistant, and it writes your setup as one block of text: classes and when they meet, the calendar, terms, what a grade is made of, how you grade, IB criteria and boundaries, rubrics, saved comments and learning goals.
Paste the block back and press Check it. You see what would change, untick anything you don’t want, and can undo it afterwards. Anything about students is left out and said so.
Copy my setup gives your own setup as the same kind of text, for a colleague to start from. The welcome has a line that leads here.
1.27.23: Take my work with me now carries your Planner too: lessons, units, timetable and their files. Bring work in takes it in. A Planner already in use only receives the lessons and files it doesn’t have, so nothing there is replaced.
If Grading Studio ever moves to a new web address, the old address tells you and shows the three steps for taking your work along. Help has an answer for it.
1.27.22: Attendance has a choice for a student who is away when you don’t know why yet: Absent, reason unknown. Change it to Absent, excused when you hear the reason. It is still four choices, and days you saved before keep their marks. Look back lists the absences that still have no reason.
1.27.21: Comments are easier to work with. Change a comment’s color at any time, even while typing it: its box has a Color row, and a Highlight row when it is on highlighted words. Text boxes and Quick mark comments have colors too.
Drag a new comment’s line up or down before you type a word, and press Enter to finish a comment or text box. Shift Enter starts a new line.
1.27.20: Feedback-only work no longer says 0 of 20 scored. A formative activity counts the students whose feedback is complete, on its card, in Find, Today, To do, the Grades box and the grade sheet, and says Ready to return once everyone has feedback.
1.27.19: Presentations and videos. On an assignment’s card, Add papers… now has No papers: presentations or videos…, which gives every student on the roster a notes page to write on while you watch. Pick lined, your rubric’s rows, two columns or blank.

On a student’s page, + Add has A video…: paste a link from Google Drive, YouTube or anywhere else, and tick the partners in it. One set of notes and one grade covers the group. Only the link is kept, so the video stays where it is.
Play here shows the video above the notes page; Open in its own window puts it beside the app. + Add also has A notes page… for one more page at any time.

Clips: under a video, + Clip saves a part worth showing, as a start time, an end time and a title. Show to the class plays it full screen with the title and without the student’s name, and Clips to show the class under Setup plays them one after another.
1.27.18: The app no longer assumes your AI assistant is Claude. Settings, Working with AI lets you pick Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, Copilot, another name, or none, and buttons and hints use that name. If you already used the app, yours stays Claude.
Planner, Timetable has a Slides section: the agenda on slide 2 and keeping text between 28 and 36 pt are both on, and each can be turned off.
The week shows Saturday, or Sunday in front of Monday, when a class meets then. Short dates follow your computer's day and month order.
1.27.17: Answer notes for quizzes: type each question's answer in Quiz boxes, and it goes on the returned papers in a gold note labelled Answer, by each question a student lost points on. In Quiz boxes, Answer notes can be set to every question or off.
1.27.16: The grade sheet shows the score you gave each paper in Grading Studio, the same number as the score panel, with extra credit and the retake that counts. Grades found typed on the papers only show for papers with no score yet, or when you tick Also show grades found on the papers. A score stamp already on a paper now changes when the score does.
1.27.15: Copy one quiz answer as a picture: in Quick mark, press P or ⧉ Copy on an answer, then paste it into Claude to ask whether it is right. The picture shows only that answer, with the question and your answer key on top. The name, score, your mark and the file name are left off, and name covers are painted in, but the student’s handwriting and words still show.
1.27.14: Points written on a paper can have their own color. In Quick mark’s Colors menu, or Settings, Marking, Mark colors: the ✗ color as before, one color of your own, or By credit, with full points in the check color, part in amber and none in the ✗ color.
1.27.13: Share lesson file, under More in a lesson: one small file with the slides, notes, pictures, materials and finished PowerPoint. Open it with Import a lesson on another computer, or give it to another teacher.
Which classes and days a lesson is on, taught notes and comments for Claude stay behind, and opening one never replaces a lesson you have.
1.27.12: A to-do list. To do in the sidebar holds your own list beside what the app noticed from your work: papers to mark, papers to hand back, a class with no lesson planned, missing work to chase. Those go by themselves when the work is done, and each kind can be switched off.
Type a to-do the way you would say it, like “Call Bram’s parents friday”, and it picks out the day, the class and the student. Press N anywhere outside a paper to add one.
A to-do can have a day, a class, a student or assignment it goes with, a repeat and a note. Today shows a short card of what is overdue or due today.

Week, at the top right of To do, shows your week: each line on its day, under the class that meets then. Type in a day to add one, or drag a line to another day. Anything not done moves to today on its own.
1.27.11: Groups in Present mode: shuffling no longer moves the slides or ends the lesson, and each shuffle keeps last time's groups apart.
Change groups by hand: drag a name to another group, or click a name and then a group. Make my own starts with empty groups, and Undo or Ctrl Z takes back a move or a shuffle.
The Present timer keeps running after you finish or leave full screen, in the corner of the Planner, and comes back on the slides when you present again.
1.27.10: Finding names on its own is now off unless you turn it on, in Settings, Marking, Name covers. Only the boxes you draw in Check the covers cover anything, and the check before anonymous grading lists every paper.
1.27.9: In the Planner's Timetable, Use my school’s template… picks your own PowerPoint template for slide downloads. Use the plain one goes back to the white one built in.
Save my setup file keeps your classes, meeting times, days off and slide template in one file to load on another computer.
1.27.8: Anchor papers: while you mark a summative, click High, Mid or Low under the score. The Return tab lists the three and exports them in one ZIP, each named for the assignment and its level, like “River essay - Summative High.pdf”, with student names covered.
1.27.7: Keep strong work as an example: press ☆ Example on an answer in Quick mark (or E), or pick Use as an example in the ⋯ beside a student’s name for a whole paper or part of a page. Names are covered, and your marks and the score stay off unless you switch them on. It is always optional.
The Examples tab on an assignment, and Examples in the sidebar for every class, have Show to the class, Copy picture, Download and Download as a sheet.
Examples go to your linked folder and into the take-home file with the rest of your work.
1.27.6: Returned files are named for the student, the assignment and what they are, like “Ana Lee - River essay - Graded.pdf”, or Feedback when there is no score. They still go in each student’s own folder.
To keep the names students turned in, untick Name each file by student and assignment under Options on the Return tab.
1.27.5: The gradebook can import your old scores: press Import… and choose a CSV or Excel file, or paste the cells. Each column becomes an assignment, matched to your roster.
You see everything before it is saved, and a score already in the gradebook stays unless you choose the file’s.
1.27.4: School is a new page in the sidebar for the things about your school you look up again and again: the handbook, the calendar, the bell schedule, portals, forms, who to call.
Add a link, a file (a copy is kept with your work) or a note. Name your own groups, and star the ones you open most to keep them along the top.
Drop files on the page or paste a web address. Find anything lists every resource. They are kept in your folder and take-home file, and stay when you start a new school year.
1.27.3: The class timer in Present takes minutes and seconds: type them in, or pick 0:30 and the other quick times. The menu remembers the last time you typed.
While it runs, the timer's menu adds or takes away 10 seconds or a minute, pauses, and restarts from the time you set. + and − add or take away a minute without opening the menu.
Tick Show it big to put the countdown in the middle of the screen, large enough for the back of the room.
1.27.2: In the gradebook, in-class assessments are now on the left and summatives on the right: the columns, the averages beside the term grade, and wherever you choose a type.
The order is yours to change. In Term setup, the arrows beside each type move it, and the gradebook's columns follow from left to right.

You can make your own assignment types. In Term setup, rename a type or press + Add a type (Homework, Projects, Quizzes), and give each its share of the grade. Your own setup stays as it is until you change it.
1.27.1: Undo now takes back a score as well as a mark: press Ctrl Z (⌘Z on a Mac) after a slip on a slider, a number key, or Missing, Excused or Late. Redo puts it back.
Deleting a unit, an assignment or a class shows Undo for a few seconds, and Undo puts it back where it was.

“Picked up where you left off” shows once, when you open an assignment, and no longer on Today or other pages. The note about what opened leaves by itself when you move to the next student, if every file opened.
The Next button stays in one place from student to student, and the Grade heading on a class’s Students tab is drawn properly.
Find anything answers to more everyday words: export, hand back, backup, undo, shortcuts, csv.
1.27.0: Start a new school year, in Settings, Saving and carrying. Your classes, units and assignment cards carry on, each card with its rubric and Quick mark boxes, with empty class lists and dates a year later.
This year goes into one protected file first, and the file is checked before anything is cleared. Open an archived year brings a year back from its file.
1.26.2: Rubric rows can be scored on your own scale. They start at 0 to 4 with half points, as before; when you set up an assignment you can pick any top from 1 to 10 and turn half points off.
Settings, Grading: choose the row scale new assignments start with. Assignments you already have keep theirs.
1.26.1: Activities: See, think, wonder now says it comes from Project Zero at the Harvard Graduate School of Education.
1.26.0: Seating: a new tab on each class. Pick how the room is set up, drag students to desks, and Shuffle gives everyone a new seat. A student can be kept in their seat.
Pick a name shows one student at random, and nobody twice until everyone has had a turn. Make groups deals the class into groups of any size.
While presenting a lesson, P picks a name and G makes groups. Who’s here leaves out anyone who is away today.
1.25.0: Attendance. Each class has an Attendance tab: everyone starts as present, so a day is one press for each student who is late, excused or absent, with a note if you want one.
Look back shows every saved day in one table with each student’s totals, and a student’s own page lists the days they missed.
Copy a day, or download the table as a spreadsheet, for your school’s system. Today has a line for it under each class.
If you don’t take attendance here, turn it off in Settings, Classes and rosters.
1.24.0: Retakes: a second try at the same assignment keeps the first try's score, comment and paper. Start one from the ⋯ beside Missing, Excused and Late on a paper.
You choose which try counts, for all your classes: the highest (to begin with), the latest, or the average. It is in the retake box and in the gradebook's Term setup.
A score typed into the gradebook takes a retake too: type both, like 7 > 10.
1.23.0: Scores by learning goal, if you want them. Keep your own list of goals (a skill, or a standard from your school) in Settings, Grading, or add one wherever you tag.
Tag rubric rows in Rubric setup and quiz questions in Quiz boxes. An assignment scored with just a total can carry one goal for the whole score.

Each class page gets a Goals tab: the class average on each goal with the lowest first, every student by every goal, and where each number came from. A student's own page shows their goals beside the class average.
Nothing changes until you add a first goal, and tagging never changes a score or a grade.
1.22.0: Progress sheets for parent meetings: one printed page per student with the term grade, every score, a chart of how they moved, missing work, each term's grade, the report comment and lines for notes. Find it on a class's Students list, or Progress sheet on one student's page.
Choose the term and tick what goes on it; Print opens the print window, where you can pick a printer or Save as PDF. It is made on your computer and nothing is sent anywhere.
1.21.0: Each class has a Missing work tab: every paper you marked Missing, by student or by assignment, for the term you pick.

Email reminder opens an email in your own mail app, addressed to the student and listing what they owe, for you to read and send. Email all writes one email to everyone who owes an assignment, with the addresses in Bcc. Grading Studio sends nothing itself.
Each reminder you open is noted beside the work, and Email wording… changes what every reminder says.
1.20.0: The app can speak Traditional Chinese (繁體中文). Choose it in Settings, Display, App language, or at the top of the welcome.

Like Spanish, it covers the first screens so far: the sidebar, Today, the welcome, Find anything, Help, and the feedback page students get with a returned paper. The other screens are still in English.
1.19.0: The app can speak Spanish. Choose it in Settings, Display, App language, or at the top of the welcome.
Spanish covers the first screens so far: the sidebar, Today, the welcome, Find anything, Help, and the feedback page students get with a returned paper. The other screens are still in English.
Names you typed (classes, students, assignments, rubric rows) are never translated.
1.18.0: On a tablet, a pencil draws and the pen's line is wider where you press harder. Once you have used a pencil, one finger moves the page, two fingers pinch to zoom, and a hand resting on the screen does nothing.
Settings, Marking has a new Tablet and pencil section: choose what a finger does on the paper, or turn off the wider line.
On a touch screen the tools, the student rows and the score buttons are larger.
1.17.0: Report comments: a new tab on each class's page drafts a comment for every student from your own gradebook, rubric scores and the comments you wrote on their papers. Edit each one, tick it done, then copy or download them all.
The drafts are put together on your computer from sentences you can change under Wording. Nothing about a student is sent anywhere.
1.16.0: Help is in the sidebar: short answers to the questions teachers ask most, from opening a set of papers to moving your work to another computer.
Find anything answers questions too. Type a few words, like “late paper” or “backup”, and the answer is in the list.
1.15.0: A picture dragged onto a slide that has text now sits beside the text, in a new Text + picture layout.
Drag several pictures in at once and each gets its own slide. Let a picture go on any slide in the list on the left to put it there.
New Full picture layout: the picture fills the whole slide.
1.14.0: Extra credit: points or a percent on one paper, and extra credit entries in the gradebook that add to the term grade or the in-class average.

The gradebook shows each type's average (summative, in-class) right beside the term grade, kept in view as you scroll. Averages only shows just those columns, and Whole year splits each term the same way.
Leave out… lets you untick students to see the class averages without them. Their own grades don't change, and nothing is saved.
1.13.0: Present a lesson from the Planner, or from Today when its class is on now or next: its slides fill the screen, and the arrow keys or a clicker move through them.
While presenting, A shows the agenda to tick off, T starts a timer the class can see, N shows your notes and B blanks the screen.
The bar shows how many minutes the class has left, from your timetable.
After a lesson is taught, one line says where the class got to. It shows on the lesson and on the week, and presenting again picks up there.
1.12.0: A returned paper starts with a feedback page: the score, each rubric row with the level given and what that level means, your comment, and every comment on the paper with its page number.
It is on unless you turn it off under Options on the Return tab. Your own pages are not changed, and bringing an export back in opens only those.
1.11.0: The Planner’s sections are in the sidebar: Calendar, Units, Past lessons, Activities and Rubrics. The row of tabs across the top is gone.
A lesson has a lighter top: its name, its classes, its status and Download. Copy for Claude, Versions, the upload and the links are under More.
Comments shows above a lesson once it has one.
1.7.0: Home is now Today: the classes you teach today with the lesson planned for each, the papers waiting to be marked, and the papers ready to hand back.
What the class needs next: after a set of papers is scored, Today shows the weakest rubric row and how many students to sit down with.
A class page is quieter. Click anywhere on an assignment’s row to open it; the only blue button is the one that adds an assignment.
Forget, and the other ways to open papers, moved into the ⋯ menu on each row.
1.6.0: A new browser opens on three questions (your classes, how you grade, where work is kept) and starts with nothing of anyone else’s in it.
A sample class of made-up students, with papers to mark, for trying things out. Remove it from Home when you’re done.
The app uses the name of your own school system. Choose it, and how you usually grade, in Settings.
Letter grades or IB 1 to 7 can show beside the percent, with boundaries you set.
Canvas and Moodle downloads are grouped by student. The Planner works without a setup file, and downloads lessons as PowerPoint with a plain built-in template.
1.5.0: The sidebar says “Not backed up”, in amber, until a folder holds a second copy of your work. Home asks for that folder once.
Go back in time, in Settings: any assignment as it was on an earlier day, restored on its own, with Undo.
Grading Studio can be installed as an app, and it opens with no internet.
A newer version now waits until you click Update now, so nothing changes in the middle of marking.
